nodes.name: SiO2 spheres synthesis
nodes.procedure: A total of 0.6 ml of TEOS, 64 ml of isopropanol, 23.5 ml of deionized (DI) water, and 13 ml NH3·H2O was injected into a beaker with pipette and then magnetically stirred at 35°C for 1 hour. A total of 5 ml of TEOS was added dropwise into the above solution. After 2 hours of stirring, the product was collected by centrifugation and washed with DI water until the pH of solution is 7. After drying at 60°C for 24 hours, SiO2 spheres were obtained.

nodes.name: Cu silicate hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 120 mg of SiO2 was first dispersed in 60 ml of DI water through ultrasonication, and then 12 mmol of NH4Cl, 1.2 mmol of Cu(CH3COO)2, and 1.2 ml of NH3·H2O were added to the above mixture under stirring. The mixture was transferred into a Teflon-lined autoclave and maintained at 140°C for 10 hours. After the autoclave was cooled down to room temperature naturally, the product was collected by centrifugation and washed with DI water and ethanol. After drying at 60°C for 24 hours, Cu silicate was obtained.

nodes.name: Co silicate hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Cu silicate and Co silicate were prepared by a hydrothermal method using the resulted SiO2 spheres as the template. For Co silicate, 60 mg of SiO2, 24 mmol of NH4Cl, 0.6 mmol of Co(CH3COO)2, and 0.4 ml of NH3·H2O were used. The hydrothermal process was maintained at 100°C for 20 hours. [Following the same procedure as Cu silicate: dispersed in DI water through ultrasonication, added reagents under stirring, transferred to Teflon-lined autoclave, cooled naturally, centrifuged, washed with DI water and ethanol, dried at 60°C for 24 h].

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms fine Cu nanoparticles and hollow structure of SiO2 in Cu/SiO2; element mappings demonstrate uniform Cu and SiO2 distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fine Cu nanoparticles are confirmed by TEM image (fig. S6G). ... Element mappings (Fig. 2C) demonstrate the hollow structure of SiO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED reveals Cu (111) crystal face on the nanoparticles of Cu/SiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cu (111) crystal face on the nanoparticles is revealed by high-resolution TEM and SAED (fig. S6H).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD verifies Cu/SiO2 with Cu cubic crystal corresponding to JCPDS card no.70-3038.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cu/SiO2 is further verified by x-ray diffraction (XRD) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) for Cu2p, Cu LMM, and Si2p (fig. S7). The Cu cubic crystal corresponding to joint committee on powder diffraction standards (JCPDS) card no.70-3038 is demonstrated in fig. S7A.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms metallic Cu state in Cu/SiO2 and absence of Si-O-Cu bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metallic Cu state is also supported by fig. S7 (B and C). The absence of Si-O-Cu bond in Cu/SiO2 is revealed by fig. S7D.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines Cu content in Cu/SiO2 as 40.6 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu content in Cu/SiO2 is 40.6wt% according to inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge XANES spectra of Cu/SiO2 show valence state close to metallic Cu foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed by the Cu K-edge x-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra (Fig. 2D), the valence state of Cu in Cu/SiO2 and Cu catalysts is close to metallic Cu foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed Cu K-edge EXAFS spectra of Cu/SiO2 show Cu-Cu coordination at ~2.2Å and absence of Cu-O at ~1.6Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Fourier-transformed Cu K-edge extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Fig. 2E), the evident Cu-Cu coordination at ~2.2Å and the absence of Cu-O coordination at ~1.6Å in Cu/SiO2...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image and element mappings reveal morphology of hollow SiO2 spheres loaded with Co nanoparticles in Co/SiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of hollow SiO2 spheres loaded with Co nanoparticles is revealed by TEM image and element mappings (Fig. 4C).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD demonstrates Co cubic crystal and hexagonal crystal in Co/SiO2 corresponding to JCPDS cards nos. 89-4307 and 89-4308.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co cubic crystal and hexagonal crystal corresponding to JCPDS cards nos. 89-4307 and 89-4308 are demonstrated in fig. S18A.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals metallic Co state with slight surface oxidation and absence of Si-O-Co bond in Co/SiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metallic Co state with slight surface oxidation of Co/SiO2 is revealed by fig. S18B. The absence of Si-O-Co bond in Co/SiO2 is confirmed by fig. S18C.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines Co content in Co/SiO2 as 44.9 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co content in Co/SiO2 is 44.9wt% according to the ICP-AES result.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pb UPD-stripping test shows electrochemical active surface areas (ECSAs) of Cu/SiO2 and Cu are comparable with same Cu metal loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pb underpotential deposition (UPD)-stripping test reveals that, with the same Cu metal loading, the electrochemical active surface areas (ECSAs) of Cu/SiO2 and Cu are comparable (fig. S8).
